blocks.text: Former Disney boss Bob Iger allegedly impregnated an employee in the 1990s, according to an explosive new book, per the New York Times.

The newspaper has published an interview with Wall Street Journal reporter Robbie Whelan, the author of a forthcoming and reportedly unflattering biography of the Disney big cheese titled “The House of Mouse.”

According to the NYT, the book documents a consensual extramarital relationship between Iger and an “ABC marketer” that took place in the early 1990s when Iger was head of ABC and resulted in a pregnancy. Whelan reportedly writes that the woman, who was at the time rungs below Iger on the corporate ladder, allegedly “suffered through a traumatic termination procedure.”

blocks.text: Iger’s 18-year-long reign (split across two tenures) as Disney CEO ended in March, when he was replaced by parks boss Josh D’Amaro. Iger is due to attend his final Disney board meeting next week – the same day “The House of Mouse” is published.

Whelan told the Times that neither Iger nor Disney spoke to him for the book but said his publisher, William Morrow, received legal letters from Iger’s lawyer raising concerns about the tome painting a “false and defamatory” picture.
“Their instinct was to bully me,” Whelan told the Times. He said he spoke to other sources, including former Marvel CEO Ike Perlmutter, who has a frosty relationship with Iger.

“A character having an ax to grind — or a motivation is a better way of putting it — just makes him a better character,” Whelan said of his sources’ possible agendas. “It doesn’t make them disqualified.”
Variety has contacted Disney and Iger’s legal representative for comment.

In a statement to the Times, the company said: “Bob Iger is one of the most respected CEOs of his generation” pointing to his “bold creative and strategic decisions” and that he leaves Disney “stronger and more innovative.”
